references.text: God created light as the first act of creation. John connects the Word (Logos) to this original light that shines for humanity, cf. [ref:Gen 1:3|Genesis 1:3].
Job speaks of God's Spirit having created him and the breath of the Almighty giving him life. Life has its origin in God, just as John says that life was in the Word, cf. [ref:Job 33:4|Job 33:4].

The psalmist confesses that the source of life is with God, and in his light we see light. This is one of the clearest Old Testament parallels uniting the themes of life and light in God, cf. [ref:Ps 36:10|Psalms 36:10].
David confesses that the Lord is his light and his salvation. The theme of God as light for people points forward to Christ as the light of life, cf. [ref:Ps 27:1|Psalms 27:1].
Isaiah prophesies that the people walking in darkness will see a great light. This messianic promise is fulfilled in Christ, who is the light of life for humanity, cf. [ref:Isa 9:2|Isaiah 9:2].
The Lord's servant shall be a light to the nations and bring salvation to the ends of the earth. The Word, who is the light of the world, fulfills this prophecy, cf. [ref:Isa 49:6|Isaiah 49:6].
Jesus says that the Father has life in himself, and he has given the Son to have life in himself. This clarifies that life is in Christ – the Son is the source of life, cf. [ref:John 5:26|John 5:26].

Jesus declares: "I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will not walk in darkness but will have the light of life." Here Jesus himself unites the themes of life and light, cf. [ref:John 8:12|John 8:12].
Jesus says: "As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world." This confirms that he is the light that shines for humanity, cf. [ref:John 9:5|John 9:5].
Jesus says: "I am the resurrection and the life." He identifies himself as the source of life, in line with the prologue which states that life was in him, cf. [ref:John 11:25|John 11:25].
Jesus says: "I am the way, the truth, and the life." The life that was in the Word is here fully identified with Jesus' person, cf. [ref:John 14:6|John 14:6].

John writes about the Word of life who was from the beginning, and that life was made manifest. This is a direct parallel to the prologue of John's Gospel stating that life was in the Word, cf. [ref:1 John 1:1–2|1 John 1:1–2].
John writes that God has given us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. Whoever has the Son has life. This clarifies that life is in Christ, cf. [ref:1 John 5:11–12|1 John 5:11–12].
